question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for increased melanin production during pregnancy?
explanation: Elevated levels of melanocyte-stimulating hormone directly activate melanocytes to produce more pigment during gestation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h1)

question: Oestrogen contributes to pregnancy-related skin changes by causing what effect?

options.A: Increased dermal blood flow and vascular permeability
options.B: Complete cessation of sweat gland secretions
options.C: Rapid destruction of subcutaneous fat layers
options.D: Decreased production of natural skin oils

explanation: Higher oestrogen levels expand blood vessels in the skin, leading to increased warmth and visible vascular markings. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h1)

question: What is the dark midline vertical line on the pregnant abdomen called?
explanation: Linea nigra is the pigmented line that commonly develops down the center of the abdomen during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: Melasma during pregnancy typically presents in which pattern on the face?

options.A: Scattered white depigmented spots on the eyelids
options.B: Bright red circular rings across the chin
options.C: Irregular brown patches on the forehead and cheeks
options.D: Painful fluid-filled blisters around the lips

explanation: Melasma creates dark, blotchy patches symmetrically distributed over sun-exposed areas of the face like cheeks and forehead. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: Striae gravidarum on the abdomen are primarily caused by stretching and changes in what skin component?
explanation: Hormonal shifts alter collagen and elastin fibers, which tear under mechanical tension to form striae gravidarum. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: Spider angiomas develop during pregnancy due to which physiological factor?

options.A: Increased platelet aggregation in superficial skin layers
options.B: Blocked lymphatic drainage in the upper extremities
options.C: High levels of circulating oestrogen dilating small blood vessels
options.D: Reduced blood volume causing localized tissue hypoxia

explanation: Elevated oestrogen triggers the dilation of superficial capillaries, creating the characteristic spider-like vascular lesions. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience thicker hair during gestation?

options.A: Hormones prolong the growth phase of hair follicles
options.B: Blood flow to hair roots decreases significantly
options.C: Protein intake is automatically stored in hair shafts
options.D: Sebum production increases along the scalp

explanation: Pregnancy hormones keep hair in the growing phase longer, delaying the normal shedding process. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: What happens to a woman's hair shortly after childbirth?

options.A: Individual hair strands become thicker and coarser
options.B: Hair color permanently changes to a lighter shade
options.C: Mass shedding occurs as follicles enter the resting phase
options.D: Hair growth stops completely for at least one year

explanation: Postpartum hormone drops cause delayed shedding to happen all at once, known as telogen effluvium. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is characterized by severe itching most notably on which body parts?
explanation: Bile acid accumulation in cholestasis causes intense pruritus that classically affects the palms and soles first. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h5)

question: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy most commonly first appear in which location?

options.B: On the soles of the feet

explanation: These itchy bumps usually originate within the striae gravidarum on the abdomen before spreading. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h5)

question: What is a common immediate skin response observed during active labour?
explanation: High physical exertion and metabolic activity during labour trigger heavy diaphoresis. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h6)

question: How do striae gravidarum typically change months after childbirth?

options.A: They expand and develop fluid-filled blisters
options.B: They fade into silvery-white, less prominent scars
options.C: They disappear completely without a trace
options.D: They turn into dark brown raised nodules

explanation: Although stretch marks remain permanent, their color softens from red-purple to a silvery-white hue over time. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h6)

question: Which symptom reported by a pregnant woman requires immediate medical reporting due to potential foetal risk?

options.A: Severe generalized itching without an obvious rash
options.B: Gradual darkening of the linea nigra on the abdomen
options.C: Softening and mild brittleness of the fingernails
options.D: Development of small spider angiomas on the cheeks

explanation: Generalized pruritus points toward intrahepatic cholestasis, which demands prompt medical evaluation for foetal safety. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)

question: What is a primary goal of nursing education regarding normal dermatological changes in pregnancy?

options.A: Prescribing topical steroid creams for every reported skin lesion
options.B: Reassuring mothers about benign changes while teaching warning signs
options.C: Encouraging surgical removal of vascular markings before delivery
options.D: Preventing all forms of hormonal hyperpigmentation with strict diets

explanation: Nurses help alleviate anxiety by explaining normal pigment shifts while ensuring dangerous conditions are identified early. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)
